idiom_name: async URLSession data(from:) with Codable decoding
implementation_notes: URLSession is the connection - URLSession.shared for simple cases or a configured session (ephemeral, background, delegate) - and the gateway is a protocol plus a struct (or actor) whose async methods call data(from:)/data(for:) and decode with JSONDecoder into domestic types. Apple documents three delivery styles on the same API (async methods, completion handlers, delegates); the async style turns the foreign call into a single await and lets errors surface as thrown values, which the gateway maps into one domestic error enum covering URLError, non-2xx status and decoding failures. Declare the domestic protocol so tests can inject a double, and isolate mutable state in an actor rather than sharing a class across tasks.
pitfalls: A URLSession keeps a strong reference to its delegate until the app exits or the session is invalidated: per-gateway sessions with delegates that are never invalidated leak memory (Apple states this explicitly).
Cancellation is cooperative - a cancelled Task does not cancel the transfer by itself, so check Task.checkCancellation()/CancellationError before translating a dead result.
JSONDecoder maps foreign key names straight into domestic types: use CodingKeys or an explicit mapping type so the foreign vocabulary does not become your model.
URLSession.shared cannot be configured per gateway: sharing it silently inherits the app-wide cache, cookie and timeout policy.

variants.name: Callback gateway over dataTask(with:completionHandler:)
variants.implementation_notes: Before Swift concurrency, or where callers are themselves callback-based, the gateway is a class whose methods start a URLSession dataTask(with:completionHandler:) and deliver the domestic result through a Result<[Slot], BookingError> completion; the handler runs on the session's delegate queue, so any actor or main-thread state must be hopped explicitly. This is the shape to expect in pre-5.5 codebases and in code that must support older deployment targets, and it needs the same translation discipline: transport, HTTP status and decoding failures arrive in different parameters and must be funnelled into one error type. The async variant is preferable whenever the deployment target allows it.
pitfalls: A URLSessionDataTask does nothing until resume() is called - the most common silent failure of this form.
The completion handler runs on the session's delegate queue (a background queue), so UI or actor-isolated state must be hopped explicitly.
Capturing self strongly inside the handler keeps the gateway and its session alive; use [weak self] where the gateway owns the session.
